name: Hebeloma cylindrosporum

ecology.substrate: coastal dune sand around pine roots

size_cm.source: Hebeloma Project, Hebeloma cylindrosporum: species description and distribution, hebeloma.org
size_cm.note: cap diameter 12 to 40 mm over 42 collections (extremes 10 to 64 mm); stem 28 to 66 mm long, 3 to 6 mm wide

notes: Medium-distance fringe type at genus level [13]. A lab model that completes its life cycle in culture; a sequenced genome and field-mapped short-lived individuals are reported (unchecked).

tip_speed.note: Field figure, not a culture rate: two genets in a pine forest site widened their territories by about 0.45 to 0.60 m per year between 1993 and 1997 (Gryta H, Debaud JC, Marmeisse R 2000, Population dynamics of the symbiotic mushroom Hebeloma cylindrosporum: mycelial persistence and inbreeding, Heredity 84:294-302 (https://doi.org/10.1046/j.1365-2540.2000.00668.x; abstract read through Europe PMC)). Midpoint 0.525 m/year spread over all 8,760 hours of the year = 60 um/h. This is a year-round average, so the rate at the optimum temperature is probably higher. No agar growth rate was found

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

cold_drop.note: Fruited in flasks with Pinus pinaster at a constant 18 C, starting about 1.5 months after inoculation; a 5-day thermal shock of 6 C up or down did not change the number of fruit bodies, only their timing (Debaud JC, Gay G 1987, New Phytologist 105:429-435, https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1469-8137.1987.tb00880.x; abstract read through Europe PMC). So no temperature drop is needed
